html:
The Saint Thomas Christians are the old Christian community of Kerala in south India, one of the oldest in the world outside the Mediterranean. Their tradition says the apostle Thomas landed near Muziris in 52 CE, founded seven churches and was killed near today's Chennai. That cannot be proved, but Christians were certainly living on the coast by the 6th century, when the traveller Cosmas Indicopleustes reported them.

The route was the monsoon sea trade with the Roman world and the Gulf. The community looked to the Church of the East in Persia for its bishops and prayed in Syriac, a form of Aramaic. Local kings gave it rights recorded on copper plates, and its members lived as a high-ranking trading caste among Hindu neighbours.

The Portuguese, who arrived with Vasco da Gama, tried to bring them under Rome. A synod at Diamper in 1599 burnt Syriac books. In 1653 a large part of the community swore at the Coonan Cross never to obey the Jesuits, and the church split.

Today there are several churches, Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant, with a few million members in Kerala and abroad.
